meta.title: Code Blue
meta.notes: Celeste POV rewrite. Canon layout: long narrative + separator + CHOICES block with pill labels + long descriptions. ASCII-only.
meta.blurb: Authority is earned in blood and silence. As Dr. Celeste Marlowe, you do not prove yourself. You maintain control. But every new intern, every glance, every compromise tests how much power you truly have.

S01.text:
The ER does not intimidate you anymore.

It hums. It breathes. It bends around the people strong enough to command it.

You walk through the bay and the rhythm adjusts. Nurses pivot without being asked. Residents quiet when you enter. The room recognizes hierarchy.

Dr. Celeste Marlowe. Attending.

You earned that title the hard way.

A new intern stands near the trauma board, trying not to look overwhelmed. He adjusts his badge like it might anchor him.

You clock him once. Posture. Hands. Eyes. He wants to be seen.

Down the hall, another intern laughs too loudly. Confidence without calibration.

The night nurse moves through it all with surgical efficiency, catching mistakes before they become lawsuits.

You feel it before it happens.

The shift is going to test someone.

The question is who.

----------------
CHOICES
1) TEST THE INTERN - You push him early and see what he is made of. Pressure reveals competence and ego.
2) WATCH QUIETLY - You observe before acting. Control begins with information.
3) STABILIZE THE FLOOR - You focus on tightening the room before chaos finds it.
4) ENGAGE THE NURSE - You align with your strongest support first.

S02.text:
You move toward the intern without warning.

You hand him a chart mid-stride and do not slow down.

"Keep up," you say.

You do not explain. You do not soften it.

You watch him skim vitals while walking. He hesitates once, then recovers. Good.

In the trauma bay, you take control in three sentences. The patient stabilizes under structure.

You glance at him again.

He is not afraid.

That interests you.

----------------
CHOICES
1) PUSH HARDER - You increase pressure and see if he cracks.
2) OFFER GUIDANCE - You calibrate him instead of crushing him.
3) STAY NEUTRAL - You let the shift decide his fate.
4) CHALLENGE PUBLICLY - You test him in front of the team.

S03.text:
You stay back.

Observation is power.

You watch who gravitates toward the intern. Who ignores him. Who sizes him up.

The rival intern circles like he smells competition.

The nurse watches you instead.

You realize something.

This is not about medicine yet.

It is about positioning.

----------------
CHOICES
1) STEP IN LATE - You intervene at the critical moment.
2) LET THEM STRUGGLE - Growth requires discomfort.
3) ALIGN WITH NURSE - You consolidate power.
4) CALL OUT MISTAKE - You assert dominance early.

S04.text:
You recalibrate the floor.

Orders are clarified. Charts are tightened. The noise narrows.

The intern notices. He watches how you hold the room without raising your voice.

Power does not shout.

It waits.

A monitor spikes.

There it is.

----------------
CHOICES
1) TAKE COMMAND - You run the code yourself.
2) HAND IT OFF - You test someone else under pressure.
3) SPLIT CONTROL - You share authority carefully.
4) OBSERVE FIRST - You read the room before acting.

S05.text:
You align with the nurse.

She respects strength.

You exchange a look that says the same thing: no one embarrasses this department tonight.

You notice a small documentation shortcut.

You could ignore it.

You could correct it.

You could weaponize it later.

----------------
CHOICES
1) CORRECT QUIETLY - You protect standards without humiliation.
2) IGNORE IT - Loyalty buys you leverage.
3) ADDRESS PUBLICLY - You reinforce authority.
4) REMEMBER IT - Information is currency.

S06.text:
The patient crashes.

The monitor screams.

The room fractures.

You do not.

Orders leave your mouth clean and precise. Hands move. The intern reacts faster this time.

You catch a subtle error before it compounds.

The patient stabilizes.

Afterward, the intern looks at you differently.

Not intimidated.

Measuring.

You feel it.

The line between authority and attraction is thinner than policy admits.

----------------
CHOICES
1) KEEP IT PROFESSIONAL - You protect both careers.
2) LET TENSION BUILD - You allow subtext.
3) MENTOR DIRECTLY - You guide him intentionally.
4) CREATE DISTANCE - You step back before it complicates.
